record.question:
A company hires a third-party auditing SaaS provider that operates from its own AWS account and serves many customers. The provider needs a defined set of read-only API operations in the company’s account. The company prohibits shared long-term credentials and wants to prevent the provider from accidentally using its role for another customer.

Which access configuration should the company use?

options.text: Create a cross-account role trusted by the provider and require its customer-specific external ID. Attach AdministratorAccess to cover any audit request.
Create a least-privilege IAM user and give its access key and secret key to the provider for recurring audits.
Create a least-privilege audit role that trusts the provider’s designated AWS principal and requires the provider-generated external ID for this customer. Have the provider call STS AssumeRole.
Create a least-privilege role with a wildcard principal and require the external ID as the sole condition for assuming it.

explanation.text:
<<3>> combines temporary credentials, narrowly scoped permissions and a trust condition binding the request to the correct customer. The provider must also authorize its calling principal to assume the role. The external ID addresses the confused-deputy risk when one service operates for multiple customers.

<<1>> grants far more access than the audit requires. <<2>> distributes persistent credentials and violates the stated constraint. <<4>> treats the external ID as a secret password while leaving the trusted principal unrestricted. External IDs are not secrets and do not replace principal restrictions.

Keep the trust policy and permissions policy conceptually separate: trust controls who can obtain a session, while permissions control what that session may do.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_third-party.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole.html

diagram_alt: A policy gate requires the correct principal and customer external ID before granting a scoped temporary session.

sources.supports: Third-party roles, customer-specific provider-generated external IDs and least privilege.
AssumeRole returns temporary credentials and cross-account access requires caller authorization and target trust.

editorial_notes: Added a genuine confused-deputy requirement and replaced a duplicate unrestricted-user distractor with external-ID-only trust.
